title: ToolApiV1dot2
description: K-09 Tool API v1.2, a minor version for journey 4 (T-051; 02-contracts K-09 version table, row v1.2; section 9 F16). It only adds to v1.1 (tool-api.v1.1.schema.json, frozen by T-050 and unchanged, referred to here, which refers to v1): every v1 and v1.1 definition is here under its own name, the unchanged ones by reference; the changed ones (stepKey, given, partResult, gateAndCommit.committed, gateAndCommit.response, gateAndCommit.exchange, callName) take only new enum values, so every v1 and v1.1 exchange is a v1.2 exchange. Added: the calls of journey 4 (A4-01 to A4-99, B4-01 to B4-115; S12-01 to S12-05 and S12-28 with journey 4): matchService (gives service), setWhoFor (who_for), setReachWay (reach_by), addCustomer (customer), setPrice (price_known, visit_fee), quoteFromPhotos (quote), showTimes (times), saveTime (choice, time_saved), extendTime (Q-12's one extension, round 2), joinWaitlist, sendSecureLink (contact, link), checkPlace (place, address) and saveSecurePage (access, answers). Each key journey 4 writes is written by exactly one call, named in that call's request description with its step ids (02-contracts section 8; README 'v1.2', 'Each key's one call'). Round 2 (the lead's rulings DL-162, on ops/cards/T-051.md) adds, still only to v1.2's own definitions: the owner's changed price stored before its read-back (quoteFromPhotos change and changeReadBack), the links the master gives (linkIssued: a teen's parent link, a quote's times link, the photos link and its page, the pricing page's quote message), the adult who meets the pro (sendSecureLink for meetsPro, saveSecurePage meetsProYes), C3's 15 minutes only for the customer's own AI's instant money booking (saveTime's door, extendTime), screen 2's categories at A4-80, both flows' ways and the place pick, checkPlace naming its way, addCustomer's way and age band, a bounded waitlist with a texts-off answer, and an AI's place kept only as a matched town or ZIP (README 'v1.2', 'Round 2'). Round 3 (the lead's rulings DL-171) states one rule for who a saved time is held for (an agent caller's save for its agent token, a page's or a turn's for the booker's mobile on file) and has extendTime decide from that stored holder, refusing every time held for an agent token until a frozen field records the hold's door (notExtendable; README 'v1.2', 'Round 3'). K-16 v1, K-17 v1, K-27 v1 and K-30 v1 are frozen on main: the calls name their tables, columns and calls, never redefine them. Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

partResult.title: PartResult
partResult.description: What the gate did with one part, as v1.1 (arch 02 line 121; arch 06 lines 295 to 309), with one change: gives may also name the keys journey 4 gives (journeyFourKey; v1.2), so a turn that commits a journey 4 step's write names the keys it wrote. Every v1 and v1.1 part result is a v1.2 part result.

part.description: The part's index in the decide result's parts (K-02 v1 decideResult.parts).

choiceId.description: The choice the part chose or entered (K-02 v1 choose or enter), or null for another verb.

result.description: committed, stopped, dependsOnStopped, held, asked or noAction, as v1 (README 'Limits 1 to 6 at the gate').

limits.description: Each of limits 1 to 6 with its result, as the gate span logs them (K-08 v1 limitResult).

stoppedBy.description: For stopped, the limit that failed and its outcome; null otherwise.

gives.description: For committed, the keys the part's step gives that this commit wrote (A-keys.md, B-keys.md; arch 12 line 590): a key of journeys 1 and 2 (setupKey), of journey 3 (journeyThreeKey) or of journey 4 (journeyFourKey, v1.2: README 'v1.2', 'Each key's one call'), including those of the automatic steps its walk passes (arch 03 line 191); empty otherwise.

dependsOnPart.description: For dependsOnStopped, the part it depends on; null otherwise.

anyOf.description: The index of the stopped part it depends on.

gateAndCommit.response.title: GateAndCommitResponse
gateAndCommit.response.description: committed for a turn's decided texts or core actions (gateAndCommit.committed, v1.2: its parts may name journey 4's keys); fired for a clock's firing (as v1; K-05 v1 fireClock.response).

gateAndCommit.committed.title: GateAndCommitCommitted
gateAndCommit.committed.description: Committed, as v1.1; v1.2 changes only the parts' items, whose gives may name journey 4's keys (partResult).

repeated.description: true when this turn id had committed before: nothing was written and the first commit comes back (K-05 v1 commitTurn).

parts.description: One result per decide part, in order; empty for a core-only turn.

planner.description: The planner's verb as committed; null when no planner ran, or when code refused its output.

core.description: One result per core action, in the request's order (v1.1's coreResult).

written.description: What the commit wrote (K-05 v1 commitResult).

effects.description: Effect rows written in the commit, to run after it (K-07 v1; K-05 v1.1).

journeyFourKey.title: JourneyFourKey
journeyFourKey.description: A needs and gives key journey 4 gives, as the step index prints it (A-keys.md and B-keys.md, section 4; A-J4.md, B-J4.md), with the one call that writes it in journey 4 (README 'v1.2', 'Each key's one call'; 02-contracts section 8 its home): service (A4-81, B4-114: matchService), who_for (A4-80, B4-92: setWhoFor), place (B4-77: checkPlace), reach_by (A4-82, B4-93: setReachWay), customer (A4-23, B4-25: addCustomer), price_known (A4-06, A4-12, B4-07, B4-13) and visit_fee (A4-13, B4-14: setPrice), quote (B4-09: quoteFromPhotos), times (A4-14, A4-33, A4-62, A4-68, B4-15, B4-84, B4-85, B4-89: showTimes), choice (B4-16) and time_saved (A4-21, B4-23: saveTime), contact (A4-42) and link (B4-29: sendSecureLink), address (B4-30: checkPlace), access and answers (B4-34, A4-65: saveSecurePage). who_for, reach_by, times and customer at a booking the business adds stay journey 3's (confirmBusinessBooking, A3-30, B3-08).

stepKey.title: StepKey
stepKey.description: A key a step gives: journeys 1 and 2's (setupKey, v1), journey 3's (journeyThreeKey, v1.1) or journey 4's (journeyFourKey, v1.2).

given.title: Given
given.description: What an exchange assumes before its request runs, as v1.1 (seeds, the fixtures run first, the clock, what it states), with one change: a stated step may give journey 4's keys (stepKey; v1.2), which the named rule givesJourneyFourKeys checks. Every v1 and v1.1 given is a v1.2 given.

seeds.description: Seed fixtures of the frozen table parts, as <folder under contracts/db-schema>/<file>.

after.description: Fixtures of this folder whose requests run first, in order.

now.description: The time the call reads 'now' at (the fake clock on staging: BP 9.4).

stated.description: What the fixture states: for a limit fixture, the limit that fails, the kind of its outcome and its action; for a step's fixture, the step and the keys it gives (A-keys.md, B-keys.md; journey 3's from v1.1, journey 4's from v1.2); null otherwise.

note.description: Anything else the exchange assumes, in plain words.

customerSideCaller.title: CustomerSideCaller
customerSideCaller.description: Who may call a journey 4 call on the customer's side (README 'v1.2', 'Callers'): the handle actor's turn in the person's own chat with Rosie's number (door chat; caller.kind turn: the write is the chosen choice's effect inside gateAndCommit, checked by limits 1 to 6), the booking page (door page; caller.kind page, through K-21's server) or the customer's own AI (door ai; caller.kind agent, through the Agent API, K-20). Never the console or a job: a booking's own answers come from its own people (arch 02 line 129: 'The same calls serve texts, secure pages and outside AIs under the same limits').

wayOffered.title: WayOffered
wayOffered.description: One of a service's ways (K-25 v1 service_money: the place it is done, its flow and its money path), with its version and its price now, as matchService answers it and A4-01, B4-01 and B4-02 pick from. Round 2 (DL-162 ruling 6; action-layer FAIL 6): every active way of the service, in both flows, each with its own price, since 'Both' is two rows and the customer 'sees both prices first' (K-25 v1 service_money.place; A4-01; B4-02: 'at the shop for $35, or at your home for $75').

serviceMoneyId.description: K-25 v1 service_money.id, of the matched service.

flow.description: K-25 v1 service_money.flow: A, the customer comes to the business (a shop or office, a meeting spot, or video or phone); B, the business goes to the customer. A way of the other flow than the request's is picked with matchService's place pick, which moves the request to that flow (README default 75).

place.description: K-25 v1 service_money.place, as stored: business, customer, meeting_spot or video (A4-01, B4-01).

path.description: K-25 v1 service_money.path, price|before|after (one of the master's 28 for the flow; K-30 booking_lines_path_form).

price.description: The price resolver's set price for this way now (K-25 v1 price rules, the rule whose place names this way, else the service's: README default 65's resolver, for no named time or person), in integer minor units; on a visit path the visit's own promised price; null on a photos path (priced from photos: A4-07) or a visit path that promises none. Shown before any yes (B4-02; A4-05).

fromPrice.description: On a visit path, a 'from' price, only as 'from' (K-25 v1 price_rules.from_cents; A4-05); null otherwise.

optionPrice.title: OptionPrice
optionPrice.description: One price of a quote as the pro or the owner sets it (K-30 v1 quote_options): what it is (null for a quote with one option), a set price or a range's low end, and a range's high end (null for a set price), in integer minor units (A4-08, B4-09: 'a range, like $80 to $100, set at the visit inside it'; 'One quote can hold options').

linkIssued.title: LinkIssued
linkIssued.description: A link the call issued (round 2: DL-162 ruling 2, the links the master gives that round 1 issued no call for), and how it reaches its reader (README default 62, restated in default 71): in a turn, inside an outbox row whose final parts hold it (url null); to the customer's own AI or on a page, in url, once, never logged (FS line 679); from a page's commit, which writes no outbox row (v1.1 open gap 43), through a K-04 clock row due at once on the reader's handle whose clock turn writes the row (README default 72: v1.1 default 56's and v1.2 default 66's way). A secure link keeps only its code's sha256 (K-30 v1 secure_links.code_sha256; BP rule 7); its code is derived from the link's id under a Workers secret, so the slot filler fills it at finalize in the same turn or a later clock turn, and it never enters a span, a trace or the event log (README default 71; v1 default 30). Each link names its K-03 link slot (K-03 v1 slots.json); where K-03 has none that fits, README open gap 70 names the one it lacks, and the composer cannot state that link until a K-03 minor version adds it.

kind.description: secure_page (K-30 secure_links purpose secure_page: K-03 slot link.secure), photos (purpose photos, A4-07 'Add photos: rosfield.com/q/a7': no K-03 slot, open gap 70 proposes link.photos), quote (purpose quote, A4-12 'Pick a time: rosfield.com/q/r3' and A4-94 'See times: rosfield.com/q/r3e': no K-03 slot, open gap 70 proposes link.quote) or bookingPage (the business's booking page for a parent, A4-96 'Forward to a parent: rosfield.com/c/teen': no row, since nothing about the teen is kept; no K-03 slot, open gap 70 proposes link.book).

secureLinkId.description: The K-30 v1 secure_links row for a secure_page, photos or quote link; null for bookingPage, which names the business and its service only and keeps no row (README default 73).

url.description: For a page or an AI caller, the link itself, given once (rosfield.com/ then a short code; the host a config value, Q-51); null in a turn, from a page whose link goes by a clock row, and on a repeat. Never logged, never in a span (v1 default 30).

outboxRowId.description: In a turn, the row carrying the link, into that reader's open chat or to their email (RULES 4.1b; MC C9); null otherwise.

clockRowId.description: From a page's commit: the K-04 clock row due at once on the reader's handle whose clock turn writes the row carrying the link (README default 72); null otherwise.

textsOffNotice.title: TextsOffNotice
textsOffNotice.description: A yes to texts that a stopped mobile cannot give (RULES 7.5: 'Only START, or a fresh yes on a new booking from that number, turns texts back on'; MC C1; S13-32, MASTER-FLOW-A line 7242), so no K-29 consent is written and the person hears only that texts to that number are off and how START turns them back on: K-01's fixed line stopLaterReply (Q-01: 'Texts are off. Reply START, or call the business.'; its words wait on Jay). In a turn as an outbox row in that person's own chat; on a page, whose commit writes no outbox row (v1.1 open gap 43), shown by the page itself, outboxRowId null (v1.1 default 50's rule; STATE note 9: no answer holds textsOff with a consentId).

savedTimeCapError.title: SavedTimeCapError
savedTimeCapError.description: K-05 v1 reserve's savedTimeCap (arch 05 line 247; CQ-13 '(2 per business)'): a third saved time for one mobile (across businesses) or for one agent token at one business, so nothing was held (round 2: security note c). The caller hears only when its own two saved times end, never their reservation ids or their businesses (K-05 lists them; the Tool API keeps them back: RULES 4.10).

notExtendableError.title: NotExtendableError
notExtendableError.description: extendTime refused before K-05 extend, nothing changed (round 3, DL-171 ruling 1; README default 61, open gap 85): the time is not held for the booker's mobile on file, the one holder a stored fact proves to be on the standard door (a page's or a turn's save, which saveTime.exchange holds to it). agentToken: held for the customer's own AI's agent token (K-04 v1 reservations.for_agent_token; K-05 v1 savedFor.agentToken), whose door no frozen field records (K-04 v1 keeps none on the row, as K-05 v1 extend.request says; K-30 v1 booking_details.door is the booking's door, not the hold's), so C3's 15 minutes cannot be told from an AI's standard save and every such hold is refused: C3's 15 minutes are never extended (MC C3), and an AI's standard save is not extended until a K-05 or K-30 minor version records the door. booking: held for a booking (K-04 v1 reservations.booking_id), which only the business's own BOOK holds (v1.1 openRequest at door business), never a saved time this call extends.

heldFor.description: Who the time is held for (K-05 v1 savedFor): an agent token or a booking, never the booker's mobile, whose holds extendTime extends.

timeOffered.title: TimeOffered
timeOffered.description: One time on the times card (A4-14, B4-15 and their kinds A4-33, A4-62, A4-68, B4-84, B4-85, B4-89): the person, session, space or vehicle it is with (K-04 v1 resources), the time to reserve (K-05 v1 during: for an arrival window, the reserved time that also holds the job's length, K-30 README 'Times'), the zone it is shown in (the visit's, else the business's: CQ-05), the arrival window the card says for times window, and its exact price for that time and person (arch 05: 'exact prices'; K-25 v1 price rules, staff prices included), or a from price on a visit path, never shown as a set price (A4-05).

optionId.description: The time's option id on the card (K-03 v1 option id; in a turn the times card's open question's option, K-04 v1 open_questions.options).

resourceId.description: K-04 v1 resources.id, this business's: a worker, room, vehicle or class session.

during.description: The time to reserve (K-04 v1 reservations.during).

arrivalWindow.description: For times window, the arrival window the card shows ('arriving 8–10am': B4-15; K-30 booking_visits.arrival_window), inside during; null otherwise.

price.description: The exact price for this time and person, in integer minor units (K-25 v1 rule 7), or null on a visit path (fromPrice) or a photos path (the quote option's price).

fromPrice.description: On a visit path, the 'from' price (K-25 v1 price_rules.from_cents), only as 'from'; null otherwise.

seatsLeft.description: For a seat in a session, the seats left (K-04 v1 class_seats: capacity less taken; A4-33, B4-89); null otherwise.

readBackYes.title: ReadBackYes
readBackYes.description: The exact yes to a question or read-back (arch 01 line 89; arch 06 line 303): in a turn, the open question it answers and the reply's event (its words and versions are the open question's, K-04 v1 open_questions); on a page, the confirm tap's event, the words being what the page server showed from its session (K-21; v1.1 default 52), never the browser's.

exactWords.description: The words shown, as the page server kept them with its session (K-21), never the browser's.

wrongDetailsError.title: WrongDetailsError
wrongDetailsError.description: S12-05 ('The AI sent wrong details'): a service or a price the customer's AI or page sent is not this business's as listed now (K-25 v1), so nothing was written and nothing held; the follow-ups (S12-06 switches to the right service, S12-27 answers with the real price) are K-09 v1.10's, and the caller asks again with today's list.

what.description: service (not listed, or not this way's) or price (not the price for that time, person and way now).

overBookingLimitError.title: OverBookingLimitError
overBookingLimitError.description: S12-28 ('Stops bookings over a phone or address limit', pf.safety; S12-23's branch): the plug-in's limit of open bookings per phone or per address is reached, so nothing was held and Rosie's team gets a review item (v1's openReviewItem, S12-28; README 'v1.2' default 64). To the caller only that the booking can't go on now, with no reason (as S11-62's customerBlocked).

reviewItemId.description: The team review item opened (K-37 v1 review_items), never shown to the caller's AI.

quoteStateError.title: QuoteStateError
quoteStateError.description: The quote is not in a state this stage takes (K-30 v1 quotes.state: a price only while pricing; an owner's answer only while with_owner; a send only once priced and, where an OK was asked, OK'd), so nothing was written (limit 4: arch 06 line 305).

notReachableError.title: NotReachableError
notReachableError.description: The link cannot go the way asked, so nothing was written: noContact (no mobile or email on file for that person at this business: K-28 v1 customers), or chatNotOpen (a text into a mobile whose chat with Rosie is not open: RULES 4.1b; MC C9: Rosie never texts first). The caller gives it through the customer's own AI or page instead.

mobileRequiredError.title: MobileRequiredError
mobileRequiredError.description: The reach card has no mobile, and one is required when the customer or their own AI books (MC C2; D103; K-28 v1 customers.mobile_handle_id; Q-07's default): nothing was written. A customer with only a landline is booked by the business (A3-19; Q-07).

geoUnavailableError.title: GeoUnavailableError
geoUnavailableError.description: The geo port answered an error (K-17 v1 geocode.errors: unavailable or rateLimited), so nothing is known about the place and nothing was written; the step's safe default holds (B4-77: ask for the ZIP; B4-30: ask again; nothing is booked until it checks).

matchService.request.title: MatchServiceRequest
matchService.request.description: Is it a service the business offers? Gives service (A4-81, B4-114; 02-contracts section 8: K-30 the booking line's service), the one call that writes it in journey 4. The request's words for the service, as typed (in a turn decide's part field, re-parsed from that text under limit 6 before any write: arch 03 line 185; arch 06 line 309; from a page or an AI their field, read first: openRequest.safetyOutcomeId, arch 02 line 129), are matched by code to this business's own listed K-25 v1 services and their ways in both flows (round 2, DL-162 ruling 6: a service offered in both places answers both ways, each with its price, A4-01, B4-02): one fits (matched, gives service), several fit (whichOne: one 'which?' and nothing written; in a turn limit 6's one question, whose answered option, K-04 v1 open_questions.answered_option_id, names the service picked), none fits (notOnList: A4-85, B4-03 'Says plainly the business doesn't do it'), or it is listed but can't be booked (cantBeBooked: A4-99, B4-117 'Declines plainly; tells the owner', v1's handOff, kind other, in the same commit). How code matches the words (the names on the list, or Q-42's meaning index) is C-099's (v1.1 open gap 39); never a guess. The matched service's own home is K-30 booking_lines.service_id, which saveTime writes when the time is saved (K-30 README writer table: A4-21, B4-23); until then it is kept as README default 57 says (open gap 54). The place pick (place, round 2: A4-01 '1 At the shop, 2 At my home', B4-02 '1 At my home, 2 At the shop', A4-15 'Wants the other place') takes one of the ways this call answered, checked again against today's list (wrongDetails otherwise: S12-05), keeps it as README default 57 says, and gives no key (A4-01 and B4-02 give none); when the way picked is the other flow's, it moves the request to that flow in the same commit, K-04 v1 bookings.flow compared and set on the head's version (expectVersion, limit 4) while the head is at stage entry, and the walk goes on in that flow's step graph (A4-02 'From here it's the other flow'; B4-02 '2 At the shop: the other flow goes on from there'), which closes v1.1 open gap 27 (README default 75). Primary, uncached. Business: caller.businessId, the request's; row-level security scopes every row (arch 10 line 546). Person: set on the server (K-22 v1 rule 4). Repeat: caller.requestId is the key (a turn's id in a turn); a repeat writes nothing and answers the first result. Version: reads each service's and way's version, which saveTime compares (limit 4); the place pick compares and sets the head's.

bookingId.description: The request openRequest opened at its door (K-04 v1 bookings.id, stage entry).

place.title: PlacePick
place.description: The place picked from the ways this call answered (round 2, DL-162 ruling 6): in a turn the answered option of the 'where?' question (decide's pick, its option id naming the way: README default 57), from a page or an AI the way's id, checked against today's list again.

expectVersion.description: The head's version the question was asked on (limit 4).

words.description: The service as typed, or, after a 'which?', the service picked from the candidates this call answered (in a turn the answered option of its question; from a page or an AI the candidate's id, checked against the list again).

bookingId.description: The customer's side only: a turn, the booking page or the customer's own AI.

matchService.response.title: MatchServiceResponse
matchService.response.description: Matched (gives service), which one, not on the list, can't be booked, or the place picked (round 2; gives none).

ways.description: Its active ways in both flows, each with its flow and its price now (round 2: A4-01, B4-01, B4-02 pick the place from them; K-25 v1 service_money.place 'Both is two rows ... sees both prices first').

openQuestionId.description: In a turn, the open question the walk's next asking step opened in the same commit (A4-01 or B4-02 'where?', else A4-80, B4-92), whose options and versions_read carry the service and its ways (README default 57); null for a page or an AI.

oneOf.title: ServiceNotOnList
oneOf.description: A4-85, B4-03: the reply says plainly the business doesn't do it; nothing written.

oneOf.title: ServiceCantBeBooked
oneOf.description: A4-99, B4-117: listed but not booked by Rosie (K-25 v1 services.active false, or a kind not booked: K-24 v1 picked_kinds not_booked); declines plainly and tells the owner through v1's handOff (kind other; K-36 v1 hand_offs), in the same commit; a call made alone writes the hand-off row and its message waits for CQ-44 (v1.1 open gap 43).

oneOf.title: PlacePicked
oneOf.description: Round 2 (DL-162 ruling 6): the way picked, kept as README default 57 says; flowChanged when it was the other flow's way, the head's flow then set to it at stage entry (K-04 v1 bookings.flow, the head's version raised: README default 75). Gives no key.

flow.description: The request's flow after the pick (K-04 v1 bookings.flow).

openQuestionId.description: In a turn, the open question the walk's next asking step opened in the same commit, in the request's flow after the pick, whose options and versions_read carry the way (README default 57); null for a page or an AI.

matchService.errors.title: MatchServiceErrors
matchService.errors.description: Refused, nothing written. wrongDetails: a place picked that is not one of the service's active ways now (S12-05).

matchService.exchange.title: MatchServiceExchange
matchService.exchange.description: One matchService request with its outcome.

setWhoFor.request.title: SetWhoForRequest
setWhoFor.request.description: Who it's for, and if they're 18 or older; gives who_for (A4-80, B4-92; 02-contracts section 8: the K-04 v1 booking head's booker, person served and payer with K-30), the one call that writes it in journey 4; and who's who on the booking after the save (A4-24, B4-32, with A4-25, A4-26, A4-55, A4-64, A4-89, B4-74, B4-107, B4-110, B4-112, B4-113), which gives no key. A4-80's answer (round 2, DL-162 ruling 5; frontend FAIL 5) carries screen 2's categories (FS line 652: you, a child, another adult, an adult you act for, an organization's people), the booker's own answer to 'are you 18 or older?', and for a child the once-asked 'Are you the parent or guardian?' (A4-80 lines 2113 to 2114; B4-92 lines 1881 to 1882), so the checks that can end the booking run here, before any name, number, photo or address (A4-80 line 2129): an adult you act for only where the plug-in lets someone book for that adult (A4-80 line 2127), only the person served or someone with legal papers for them where the plug-in says so (B4-100 line 1956), a child only by a parent or guardian unless the plug-in lets another adult book (README default 74). Writes the head's served_person_id and payer_person_id (the booker for themself; a new K-04 person, named as typed, for a child, another adult or an adult acted for; for an organization the booker as payer and nobody served yet, README open gap 58; never a person id the browser or the AI sends: K-22 v1 rule 4), compare-and-set on the head's version (expectVersion, limit 4); a teen who may agree alone gets a private booking (A4-90, B4-106: K-04 bookings.private, as v1's setRecordFlag sets it). The person served's age band (servedAgeBand: never an exact age, A4-80; their own answer for themself, under_18 for a child, 18_or_older for another adult or an adult acted for) goes to K-28 v1 customers.age_band of the person served, as that column stores each person's own band, when they have a row at this business (compare-and-set); else it is kept as README default 57 says: for a booker served themself until addCustomer writes their row with it (open gap 54), and for a person served who is not the booker with the request, since no v1.2 call writes their customer row (addCustomer writes the booker's: open gap 54). An unclear or refused age counts as under 18, so a parent books (A4-80; CQ-71's default). Under 13 and alone (A4-86, B4-98), a teen booking alone (A4-96, B4-108), adults only for a child (B4-99) and a booker not allowed (B4-100; an act-for or a child's booking the plug-in does not allow) give no key and keep nothing about the child or the person named (RULES 4.7): no person is written, and the request ends (K-30 booking_details.request_ended_why dropped; README default 60). saveTime.request.title: SaveTimeRequest
saveTime.request.description: The pick and the saved time; gives choice (B4-16: the pick, K-30 v1 booking_details.timing) and time_saved (A4-21, B4-23: K-04 reservations, the saved time; 02-contracts section 8), the one call that writes each in journey 4 (flow A's pick, A4-15, gives no key; in a turn the walk passes the automatic save, arch 03 line 191, so the part gives both). In one commit: K-30 booking_details.timing, set once (settime, or sentnow for 'Send someone now' where the plug-in lists it: B4-91); the time held by K-05 v1 reserve on one of two doors (round 2, DL-162 ruling 4; action-layer FAIL 3, frontend FAIL 1; README default 61): ownAi, 15 minutes, never extended, only for the customer's own AI booking a service that books at once with money due now or a card to save (MC C3; K-05 v1 door ownAi: caller agent, the K-26 v1 OK rules A4-98 reads saying it books on the yes, and the way's path taking a card, a deposit or the full price before), and standard for every other save, every caller's request the owner OKs included ('A request the owner OKs keeps the master's own rules'): held_until 10 minutes on, with one 10-minute extension offered once (extendTime, K-05 extend; Q-12; A4-21 'offers more time at least once'); and the K-30 booking_lines row, written when the time is saved (K-30 README writer table), copying the service, the way, its price rule or the quote option picked, the path, price kind, units, price, deposit, fee and currency as shown on the card (S11-54; RULES 3.7; K-30 rule 10). Who the time is held for (round 3, DL-171 ruling 1; action-layer GAP 1, runtime note a; README default 61), one rule per caller on either door: an agent caller's save is held for its agent token (K-05 v1 savedFor.agentToken), which the Tool API takes from the agent's own authentication (K-20; C-110), never from a field the caller fills (no request field carries it, and businessCaller has none), and arch 05 line 247's '2 per agent token per business' counts it (K-05 item 8); a page's or a turn's save is held for the booker's mobile on file (K-05 v1 savedFor.phoneNumber: their own K-04 phone handle, K-28 customers.mobile_handle_id, which the reach card required, MC C2; with none on file the save is mobileRequired and nothing is held), so its saved-time clock row is that mobile's handle's (K-05 item 8) and S12-04 can go into an open chat. The extension follows the holder, from which extendTime decides: a page's or a turn's save answers extendable true, its one extension not yet used; an agent caller's save answers extendable false on either door until a frozen field records the hold's door, since extendTime refuses every time held for an agent token (README open gap 85: fails closed). In a turn the pick names the times card's option, and the action layer rebuilds the card from its open question's versions_read (the same versions give the same times); a row that moved fails limit 4 (fresh times) and a time taken limit 5 (nextOpenTimes). From a page or an AI the time comes back as the card answered it and is checked again: a service, way or price that is not today's is wrongDetails (S12-05) and nothing is held; a time another customer took first is timeTaken, and the caller shows the next times or a place in line (S12-01, S12-02). Over the plug-in's limit of open bookings for a phone or an address: overBookingLimit, and Rosie's team gets an S12-28 review item (README default 64). A third saved time for one mobile across businesses (a page's or a turn's save), or for one agent token at one business (an agent's), is savedTimeCap, with only when the caller's own two end (K-05 reserve; arch 05 line 247; round 2: security note c). The time lapses at held_until by its saved-time clock row (K-05 item 8): a page's or a turn's save on its mobile's handle, whose clock turn sends S12-04's one text only into an open chat (MC C9; round 2: runtime note a, security note e); an agent caller's save by the minute sweep, whose firing has no turn and writes no outbox row (K-05 open gap 3; CQ-44), and no frozen field tells C3's door from an AI's standard save, so its lapse texts nobody on either door: on the ownAi door nothing is booked or charged and nobody is chased, so S12-04's text is not sent (MC C3), and an AI's standard save sends it neither until the door is recorded (round 3; README open gap 85). Primary, uncached. Business: caller.businessId; reserve counts a mobile's saved times across businesses and a token's at this business (K-05 item 8). Person: the head's booker; the hold is for its holder as above (K-04 reservations.for_phone_number for a page's or a turn's save, for_agent_token for an agent's). Repeat: caller.requestId is the key; the reservation id is the caller's (K-05 reserve: repeated). Version: booking_details compared and set; the reservation and line at version 1.

saveTime.exchange.title: SaveTimeExchange
saveTime.exchange.description: One saveTime request with its outcome. Only the customer's own AI's save can be on the ownAi door, 15 minutes, never extended (MC C3); a turn's and a page's save is always on the standard door, 10 minutes with Q-12's extension; an AI's save is standard too for a request the owner OKs or a service with nothing to pay or save before the visit (round 2, DL-162 ruling 4; README default 61). An AI's save is held for its agent token on either door, and no frozen field records the hold's door, so an AI's standard save answers extendable false until one does (round 3, DL-171 ruling 1; README open gap 85).

extendTime.request.title: ExtendTimeRequest
extendTime.request.description: More time for a saved time (round 2, DL-162 ruling 4; frontend FAIL 1): the one 10-minute extension Q-12 offers once before the hold ends (A4-21: 'The page warns before the saved time ends, and offers more time at least once'; B4-29: 'The time stays saved while they fill it in, with more time offered before it ends'; arch 05 line 247), through K-05 v1 extend, which raises held_until by 10 minutes, sets reservations.extended and moves the saved-time clock row with it, in one commit. Gives no key. Never for C3's 15 minutes (MC C3: 'the 15 minutes are never extended'; K-05 v1 extend.errors neverExtended). K-05 extend takes the door from its caller, since K-04 v1 keeps none on the row, so the action layer decides it from a stored fact, never from the caller's word (round 3, DL-171 ruling 1; action-layer GAP 1, runtime note a; README default 61): who the time is held for (K-04 v1 reservations.for_phone_number, for_agent_token or booking_id; K-05 v1 savedFor), which saveTime set by one rule per caller. A time held for the booker's mobile on file was saved by a page or a turn, which saveTime holds only on the standard door (saveTime.exchange; the longer doors of open gap 72 are a later minor version's), so the action layer names standard to K-05 extend and the answer says heldFor phoneNumber. A time held for an agent token (an agent caller's save, on either door) is refused before K-05 extend with notExtendable, heldFor agentToken, and nothing changes: no frozen field records its door (K-30 v1 booking_details.door is the booking's door, ai, page, chat, business or walk_in, not the hold's; booking_details.approval is decided at A4-98, after the save, from K-26 rules that may have changed since, README open gap 84), so C3's 15 minutes cannot be told from an AI's standard save, and every such hold is refused until a K-05 minor version (with the K-04 column it reads) or a K-30 one records the hold's door (README open gap 85). That fails closed: C3's 15 minutes are never extended, and an AI's standard save is not extended until the door is recorded, so saveTime answers it extendable false. A time held for a booking (only the business's own BOOK holds one: v1.1 openRequest at door business) is not a saved time this call extends: notExtendable, heldFor booking. Callers: the booking page and the secure page (caller page), the customer in their own chat (a turn) and the customer's own AI (agent), for their own booking. A longer saved time from the start (A4-21: a plan check up to 1 hour, a document up to 24 hours) is K-05's planCheck and document doors, not this call (README open gap 72). Primary, uncached. Business: caller.businessId; reservations are scoped by it. Person: the head's booker, set on the server. Repeat: caller.requestId is the key; the one extension already given answers alreadyExtended (K-05 extend: a repeat changes nothing). Version: the reservation compared and set (expectVersion, limit 4).

reservationId.description: The time saveTime held (K-04 v1 reservations.id), this booking's.
The customer's side only: a turn, a page or the customer's own AI.

extendTime.response.description: Extended: the new end (the old end plus 10 minutes), the reservation's version, and no extension left (K-05 v1 extend.response); only ever for a time held for the booker's mobile on file, a page's or a turn's save on the standard door (round 3, DL-171 ruling 1).

heldFor.description: Who the time extended is held for (K-05 v1 savedFor; K-04 v1 reservations.for_phone_number): the booker's mobile on file, the one holder a stored fact proves to be on the standard door; a time held for an agent token or a booking answers notExtendable (round 3, DL-171 ruling 1; README default 61, open gap 85). The number itself is never returned.

extendTime.errors.description: Refused, nothing changed: K-05 v1 extend's neverExtended (C3's 15 minutes), alreadyExtended (the one extension was given) and notHeld (waiting, booked, released, or its end has passed), as K-05 gives them; and the Tool API's own, notExtendable among them for a time not held for the booker's mobile (round 3, DL-171 ruling 1: every time held for an agent token, until a frozen field records the hold's door, and a booking's hold), answered before K-05 extend is called.

joinWaitlist.request.title: JoinWaitlistRequest
joinWaitlist.request.description: Joins the waitlist, or next in line for a time that's taken (A4-60, B4-64; A4-15, B4-16 'Joins the waitlist'; A4-18, B4-18 'Puts Alex next in line'; A4-33 a full class); gives no key. In one commit, with the customer's own yes to messages about it (K-29 v1 consents, kind texts, bound to the words shown and their sha256: RULES 2.5): a K-30 waitlist_entries row (the service, the session or the one person asked for, the times wanted; one open entry per person and service), and the request ends there (K-30 booking_details.request_ended_why waitlist). The times wanted are never open-ended (round 2, DL-162 ruling 8; K-30 waitlist_entries.wanted not null and waitlist_entries_wanted_bounded: 'When the time passes, they hear once'): 'any time' is sent as the stated bounded range README default 81 names, from now to the end of the seventh day in the visit's zone, else the business's (A4-19: 'the waitlist for this week'). A stopped mobile gives no yes (RULES 7.5: only START, or a fresh yes on a new booking from that number, turns texts back on; MC C1; CQ-74's default: only START clears the stopped flag; a tap on the page is neither, and a stopped number's own texts get only K-01's stopLaterReply, Q-01), so the answer is textsOff: no K-29 consent (consentId null: STATE note 9, no answer holds textsOff with a consentId), K-01's stopLaterReply shown or sent, and, since K-30 v1 waitlist_entries.consent_id is not null ('nothing about the list is sent without it'), no entry can be written without that yes: the entry the ruling keeps waits for a K-30 minor version (README default 82, open gap 71), so the request stays open (request_ended_why not set) and nothing is written. Nothing is taken or saved; when a spot opens everyone on it hears at once and the first to book gets it, as a new booking (A4-60), whose notices are journey 7's. Primary, uncached. Callers: a turn or the booking page; never an AI, whose call is never the customer's own yes (A3-03). Business: caller.businessId. Person: the head's booker. Repeat: caller.requestId is the key; an open entry for the same person and service answers repeated. Version: inserts at version 1; booking_details compared and set.

sendSecureLink.request.title: SendSecureLinkRequest
sendSecureLink.request.description: The secure link; gives contact (A4-42, flow A) or link (B4-29, flow B) (02-contracts section 8: K-30 the secure link issued; K-28 the contact it went to), the one call that writes each in journey 4. Writes a K-30 v1 secure_links row of purpose secure_page for the person (the head's booker, or the person served when it is someone else, who gets their own link for their private answers and their own yes: A4-24, A4-42), its given_via and, for text or email, the contact on file it went to (K-28 customers.mobile_handle_id or email_handle_id: one of that person's own handles, secure_links_handle_own_fk); only the sha256 of its short code is kept (secure_links.code_sha256; BP rule 7). How it goes: in a turn by text into that mobile's open chat (RULES 4.1b; MC C9: Rosie never texts first; notReachable chatNotOpen otherwise) or to the email on file, as an outbox row whose final parts hold the link, which never enters a span, a trace or the event log (v1 default 30); to the customer's own AI as given_via ai and on the booking page as given_via page, the link returned to that caller once in url (FS line 679: 'It must give an AI exactly ... the secure link'), never logged, and never by text from a call made alone, whose commit writes no outbox row (v1.1 open gap 43). The walk's automatic steps after it ride the same commit: A4-43, B4-38 the plug-in's forms go on the secure page ('Not on the business's own list': the request ends not_listed), and A4-98, B4-115 decide once whether it books on the yes or asks the owner first (K-30 booking_details.approval now or ownerok, from K-26 v1 ok_same_day, ok_new_customer, ok_dates: set once). for meetsPro (round 2, DL-162 ruling 3; B4-26, B4-27; action-layer FAIL 4, frontend FAIL 4): the adult who meets the pro, once saveSecurePage's meetsPro save named them (booking_details.meets_pro someone_else, a new K-04 person named as typed), gets their own link (K-30 secure_links purpose secure_page: 'each person served or who meets the pro gets their own', B4-27), for their mobile and their own yes to texts on it (saveSecurePage meetsProYes); it is given to the booker to forward ('Alex forwards a link'), on the booker's secure page (via page) or to the booker's own AI (via ai), with no contact (secure_links.handle_id null: that adult has no contact on file, and the booker's handle is not theirs, secure_links_handle_own_fk), never texted by Rosie ('Rosie never texts the parent on Alex's word'); it gives no key (B4-27 gives none), and no form or approval rides it (README default 83). Primary, uncached. Business: caller.businessId. Person: the link's person is named by the server from the head, never sent by the browser or the AI. Repeat: caller.requestId is the key; a repeat makes no second link and answers the first without its url, since the code is not kept (a later message that needs a link gets a new one: K-30 default 12). Version: the link at version 1; booking_details compared and set.

for.description: booker (the head's booker), served (the head's person served, when it is someone else) or meetsPro (the adult who meets the pro, K-30 booking_details.meets_pro someone_else: round 2, DL-162 ruling 3).

via.description: K-30 secure_links.given_via: text or email in a turn, ai for the customer's own AI, page on the booking page or the secure page. A meetsPro link goes only via page or ai, to the booker to forward.
Each caller its own way: a turn by text or email; the AI as ai; the booking page as page. A meetsPro link is never texted or emailed by Rosie: the booker forwards it (B4-27).

sendSecureLink.exchange.description: One sendSecureLink request with its outcome. In a turn the link goes only in its outbox row (url null); to the AI or the page only in url (no outbox row).

checkPlace.request.title: CheckPlaceRequest
checkPlace.request.description: Where the job is, flow B; gives place (B4-77: the town or ZIP checked against the travel area before any times) and address (B4-30: the street address checked on the secure page) (02-contracts section 8: K-30 booking_addresses), the one call that writes each in journey 4. area: the town or ZIP as given, geocoded (K-17 v1 geocode, kind town or zip) and checked by distance in PostGIS against the travel area of the way it names (round 2, DL-162 ruling 6; action-layer FAIL 1: serviceMoneyId, a flow B way of the matched service, whose K-25 v1 service_money.location_id is the location whose travel area it is, K-23 v1 locations: travel centre and miles, and K-30 booking_addresses.location_id, which is not null) and against the states whose form the business filled in (B4-31): inside, a K-30 booking_addresses row at position 1 with the area and that location (address null), gives place; outside, the reply says the business can't go there (B4-31) and the request ends outside_area; several matches (a town two states share), not found, or a null state: askZip, nothing written (B4-77's safe default; K-17 v1 default 8). What is kept is only the geo match's town or ZIP, never the words given (round 2, DL-162 ruling 9; security GAP 1; README default 84): booking_addresses.area is the match's own normalized town or ZIP, and a text that matches finer than a town or ZIP (K-17 v1 precision street, interpolated or exact: a street address an AI or a page put in the words) is askZip with nothing kept, so an address that passes through an AI is never saved (B4-30: 'An address an AI puts in a message is never saved'; A6-14; K-30 booking_addresses.address, sealed and secure-page-only; README default 67); matchPrecision says which. street (page only: an address never passes through an AI, A6-14; 'An address an AI puts in a message is never saved', B4-30): geocoded (kind streetAddress) and checked again; inside and in a filled-in state, the row's address sealed under the key of the person who typed it on their own link (sealed_for_person_id; K-04 v1 rule 6), its zone and state_code from the match and checked_at, gives address; a partial match (a coarser precision than asked: K-17 v1) is askAgain, nothing checked (B4-30's safe default); outside after all, the request ends outside_area. Two addresses (a move, a ride, a tow) are positions 1 and 2, each with its own check. The address and the normalized address are never returned, logged or in a span (K-17 v1 'No address in a span or log'). Primary, uncached, and the geo port. Business: caller.businessId. Person: for street, caller.personId is the secure link's person, set by the page server from the link it found by its code's hash (K-30 rule 5). Repeat: caller.requestId is the key. Version: a new row at version 1; a street check compares and sets the area row's version.

serviceMoneyId.description: The flow B way checked (K-25 v1 service_money.id of the matched service, picked as README default 57 keeps it): its location_id is the travel area's and the row's location (round 2, DL-162 ruling 6).

text.description: The words given for the town or ZIP (K-17 v1 geocode.request text): geocoded, then dropped; never kept, returned, logged or in a span. Only the geo match's own town or ZIP is kept, as K-30 booking_addresses.area (round 2, DL-162 ruling 9).

address.description: The street address as typed on the secure page, sealed on write; never returned.

allOf.description: A street address only from the secure page, for the link's own person (A6-14; B4-30).

checkPlace.response.title: CheckPlaceResponse
checkPlace.response.description: The check's result, the row, the visit's zone and the key it gave; never an address.

result.description: inside (gives the key), outside (the request ends outside_area: B4-31, B4-30), askZip (B4-77) or askAgain (B4-30).

addressRowId.description: The K-30 booking_addresses row written or checked; null when nothing was written.

zone.description: For a street checked inside, its IANA zone (the visit's: S13-03; CQ-05); null otherwise.

matchPrecision.description: The best geo match's precision (K-17 v1 precision: exact, interpolated, street, zip, town); null when nothing matched, several did, or the port failed. For an area check only a town or zip match is kept (round 2, DL-162 ruling 9).

result.description: Only inside gives a key: place for the area, address for the street. An area check keeps only a town or ZIP match: a finer match (a street address in the words) is askZip with nothing written (round 2, DL-162 ruling 9; B4-30; A6-14).

checkPlace.exchange.description: One checkPlace request with its outcome.

saveSecurePage.request.title: SaveSecurePageRequest
saveSecurePage.request.description: What a person types on the booking's secure page; gives answers (A4-65: the page's questions) and access with answers (B4-34: access, door and job notes) (02-contracts section 8: K-30 page answers, access and job notes, secure page only), the one call that writes each in journey 4; and who meets the pro (B4-26, with B4-27 and B4-105), which gives no key. answers: one K-30 v1 page_answers row per answer (kind question, note, access, entry_code, safety_need, emergency_contact, child_details, authority or photo; a question's words are the plug-in's), each sealed under the key of the person who typed it (page_answers.answer, sealedBy person_id; K-04 v1 rule 6), never edited (a resubmission is a new row and the newest wins); B4-34 carries at least one access or entry_code answer, which gives access. An entry code shows to the pro only on the visit's day (B4-34), an emergency contact is called by the business and never texted by Rosie, and none goes in a text, an email or to an AI (S13-05; RULES 4.5; B6-14). meetsPro: K-30 booking_details.meets_pro (served, someone_else or nobody_home, only where the plug-in marks the work so: B4-105), compare-and-set; for someone_else, that adult is a new K-04 person named as typed, and meets_pro_person_id is set only once their own yes on their own forwarded link is in (B4-27: 'Rosie never texts the parent on Alex's word'), so their link is sendSecureLink's for meetsPro, given to the booker to forward. meetsProYes (round 2, DL-162 ruling 3; B4-27: 'On it the parent adds a mobile and says yes to texts'): on that adult's own link, the caller's person is that adult (set by the page server from their link), and one commit writes their mobile as their own K-04 handle (a phones row and its contacts/add effect, Q-03; a number Rosie already holds is linked as theirs too, and no answer tells whether Rosie knew it: README default 68), their yes on their link as a K-29 v1 consents row of kind texts for that mobile (channel page, the booking, the exact words shown and their sha256: RULES 2.5, 7.1; bound to that link by its person and booking, since K-29 v1 names no secure link: README open gap 73), and booking_details.meets_pro_person_id, that adult, compare-and-set (K-30: 'once their own yes on their link is in'). A stopped mobile gets no yes without START, or a fresh yes on a new booking from that number (RULES 7.5; MC C1): a tap on the page is neither, so no consent is written and they see only that texts are off (textsOff, K-01's stopLaterReply, no row: the page shows it), while their mobile and meets_pro_person_id are still written, since the yes the step needs is theirs on their own link, and texts wait (B4-27: 'No yes from the parent: no texts. The business calls them, or they say yes at the door'; README default 85). photos (round 2, DL-162 ruling 2d; A4-07, A4-08, B4-08, B4-09; FS line 661): on the photos link's page (K-30 secure_links purpose photos), the customer's photos and answers for the quote, each a K-30 page_answers row (kind photo with its file reference as K-13 names it, or question or note), sealed under their key, never in a text and never through an AI ('Photos of a person or a body go only on the secure page'); gives no key (the price is B4-09's); the quote stays pricing for the pro's price (who is asked to price it, and A4-08's 'Price needed' row with the pricing page's link, is README open gap 74). Primary, uncached. Only the secure page's server side (K-21; a page's commit writes no outbox row, v1.1 open gap 43; CQ-44). Business: caller.businessId. Person: caller.personId, the secure link's person, set by the page server from the link it found by its code's hash, never by the browser (K-30 rule 5). Repeat: caller.requestId is the key. Version: answers are inserted and carry no version (K-30 rule 4); booking_details compared and set.

question.description: For kind question, the plug-in's question as shown; null otherwise (page_answers_kind_known).

answer.description: As typed (for a photo, its file reference, as K-13 names it); sealed on write, never returned.

otherName.description: For someone_else, their name as typed; null otherwise.

oneOf.title: SaveMeetsProYes
oneOf.description: B4-27, on the adult's own forwarded link (round 2, DL-162 ruling 3): their mobile and their own yes to texts, on the page, with the words the page server showed (K-21), never the browser's.

mobile.description: Their mobile, as typed on their link (K-05 v1 phoneNumber).

yes.description: Their yes to texts on their own link: the page's confirm, its exact words as the page server showed them (RULES 2.5).

oneOf.title: SavePhotos
oneOf.description: A4-07, B4-08: the customer's photos and answers on the photos link's page, for the quote (round 2, DL-162 ruling 2d).

quoteId.description: The quote the photos link was made for (K-30 quotes, state pricing).

kind.description: K-30 v1 page_answers.kind: photo (its file reference), question (the plug-in's) or note.

question.description: For kind question, the plug-in's question as shown; null otherwise (page_answers_kind_known).

answer.description: As typed, or for a photo its file reference as K-13 names it; sealed on write, never returned.

save.description: Only the secure page, for the link's own person (K-30 page_answers: secure page only).

saveSecurePage.response.title: SaveSecurePageResponse
saveSecurePage.response.description: The answers saved (ids only, never their words), who meets the pro, and the keys it gave.

answerIds.description: The K-30 page_answers rows inserted (not versioned, so not in written).

meetsPro.description: K-30 booking_details.meets_pro after a meetsPro or meetsProYes save; null for answers and photos.

meetsProPersonId.description: For meetsProYes, K-30 booking_details.meets_pro_person_id as set: the link's own person (round 2, DL-162 ruling 3); null otherwise.

handles.description: For meetsProYes, the adult's mobile handle linked (K-04 v1 handles.id), never the number; empty otherwise.

effects.description: For meetsProYes, contacts/add for a mobile not yet a Linq contact (Q-03; CQ-04), and only that kind (linq_contact_add); empty otherwise.

consentId.description: For meetsProYes, their K-29 texts yes, bound to their own link (README open gap 73); null for a stopped mobile (textsOff) and for every other save.

textsOff.description: For meetsProYes on a stopped mobile, the texts-off line the page shows itself (no row: a page's commit writes none); null otherwise (round 2, DL-162 ruling 3; RULES 7.5).

gives.description: answers (A4-65); access and answers (B4-34); none for who meets the pro, the adult's yes or the photos.

consentId.description: No answer holds the texts-off line and a consent together (STATE note 9; v1.1 default 50).

saveSecurePage.exchange.title: SaveSecurePageExchange
saveSecurePage.exchange.description: One saveSecurePage request with its outcome.

gateAndCommit.exchange.title: GateAndCommitExchange
gateAndCommit.exchange.description: One gateAndCommit request with its outcome, as v1.1, its committed answer's parts able to name journey 4's keys and its given able to state a journey 4 step (v1.2).

callName.description: Every call v1.2 holds: v1.1's and journey 4's (matchService, setWhoFor, setReachWay, addCustomer, setPrice, quoteFromPhotos, showTimes, saveTime, extendTime, joinWaitlist, sendSecureLink, checkPlace, saveSecurePage). Each has <call>.request, <call>.response and <call>.errors under $defs (02-contracts section 2 item 2), and each but plannerVerbs a <call>.exchange.
